final.answer: FT-10-1 (a Rosemount 3051) does not have a fixed failure direction — the output on failure is user-selectable, either high or low. The factory default ships with alarm = High (≥ 21.75 mA for HART 4-20 mA output; ≥ 22.5 mA for some options), with Low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA. To change the direction: for the HART 4-20 mA output (code A), select high or low failure mode with a jumper/switch on the transmitter; for the 1-5 Vdc low-power output (code M), select the alarm direction with an internal jumper (failure levels there are below 0.94 V for low or above 5.4 V for high). The direction can also be set at ordering via option codes C4/CN (NAMUR-compliant: high ≥ 22.5 mA, low ≤ 3.6 mA), CR/CS (custom levels: high 20.2–23.0 mA, low 3.6–3.8 mA, with the low alarm 0.1 mA below low saturation and the high alarm 0.1 mA above high saturation), or CT (Rosemount standard low). Note: for digital outputs (Fieldbus/PROFIBUS/wireless), no high/low analog drive applies — a failure is passed as an alert and status with the process variable.
